_comment: Generated by bin/settings-coverage (Proposal 149 §183). Each row states which runtime reads the key, from source evidence, so /admin/settings-coverage can show an operator which controls do something. Regenerate rather than hand-edit: the buckets are claims about code and drift the moment it moves.

buckets.enforced: Read by runtime code that changes behaviour.
buckets.reported: Graded by the security posture report, not enforced: the admin saves the value and /admin/security scores it, but no middleware applies it.
buckets.inapplicable: Declared in InapplicableSettings: configures a WordPress plugin, endpoint or hosting model with no counterpart here, so it is not rendered.
buckets.inert: Declared in UnimplementedSettings: the capability is real upstream and not built here, so the control renders disabled and the writer refuses it.
buckets.unenforced: A security control that is rendered and writable but referenced by no enforcement point: no middleware, policy or service reads it. Changing it records an intention and changes no behaviour.
buckets.unenforced-operator: The same problem as unenforced, one scope up: an operator-scope security control that no enforcement point reads. It is writable from /ops, not from this panel, so the risk lands on whoever administers the deployment.
buckets.wordpress: A WordPress setting. The plugin reads it from wp_options; this admin writes nvoos_tenant_settings, which the plugin never reads, so changing it here has no effect on either runtime.
buckets.stale: In the generated catalogue but defined by no source: the generator emitted it from a field since removed upstream. Regenerating the catalogue drops it.
buckets.unclassified: No reader found by the sweep. Not proven dead: the sweep matches literal key names, so a reader resolving the key through a map or a variable would not be seen. Treat as suspect, not dead.
buckets.wordpress-dynamic: A WordPress setting the plugin builds by interpolation (`$slug . '_safety_buffer'`), so the literal key never appears in the plugin source. Same store boundary as the other WordPress settings: it configures the plugin, which reads wp_options.
